lessons: Prioritize immediate, high-stakes curiosity over context; hooks that pose a direct, counter-intuitive question (e.g., 'Why do potatoes sprout from dents?') perform better than descriptive statements.
Eliminate 'Pause and guess' prompts; they consistently correlate with significant viewer drop-offs, as seen in the 'Maple Syrup' and 'Foil' videos.

Avoid redundant explanations; 'Highway Guardrails' suffered a major drop when repeating the exact same phrasing in the second drop-line, signaling to viewers that they have already heard the core point.
Keep technical definitions brief; long-winded chemical or biological explanations (as seen in the 'Fingers Prune' and 'Potatoes' drops) cause viewers to disengage before the midpoint.
Maintain high energy through the first 15% of the video; drops are most severe (20-34% loss) when the script transitions into slow setup or complex chemical terminology too early.
worst_moment_types: Literal repetition of information provided seconds earlier
Transitioning from a hook into a dense, multi-sentence technical or chemical definition
Self-evident statements that state the obvious rather than building on the hook
best_hook_types: Direct questions about everyday objects that contradict common assumptions (e.g., 'Why fresh pineapple eats you back')
High-contrast comparisons that frame two common things as fundamentally different (e.g., 'Tuna vs. Cod')
Extreme scenarios that create immediate stakes (e.g., 'Shark older than the US')
